title: Patient registration and record retrieval
description: How reliably patient information is captured, organised and found.

questions.A1: How reliably does your clinic maintain one clearly identifiable record for each patient, without duplicate or mixed-up files?
questions.A2: How consistently are a new patient's required registration details completed before the first treatment session?
questions.A3: How reliably can the treating physiotherapist find a returning patient's previous treatment history within two minutes?
questions.A4: How consistently are relevant medical reports linked to the correct patient record?
questions.A5: How reliably can staff find existing patient information without asking the patient to provide it again?

title: Treatment documentation and continuity
description: How consistently treatment is documented and understood across visits.

questions.B1: How consistently is an initial assessment recorded for each new treatment episode?
questions.B2: How consistently is a clear treatment goal recorded for each treatment episode?
questions.B3: How consistently is a dated treatment note completed on the same day as each session?
questions.B4: How consistently are the exercises or treatment activities performed during a session recorded with enough detail for the next visit?
questions.B5: How reliably can another physiotherapist understand the patient's current treatment plan from the record without needing a verbal explanation?

title: Treatment charges and payment control
description: How accurately treatment charges, collections and balances are maintained.

questions.C1: How consistently is the correct charge recorded for every chargeable treatment session?
questions.C2: How consistently is each payment recorded against the correct patient on the day it is received?
questions.C3: How reliably can staff confirm a patient's outstanding balance without manually recalculating past transactions?
questions.C4: How consistently are recorded collections checked against the payments actually received?
questions.C5: How consistently are overdue patient balances reviewed according to a defined routine?

title: Staff coordination and owner visibility
description: How well responsibilities, continuity and routine oversight work.

questions.D1: How consistently do staff follow a clear allocation of responsibility for completing patient records?
questions.D2: How reliably can routine administration continue when the staff member who normally handles it is absent?
questions.D3: How consistently are patients who stop attending before their planned treatment is completed identified for review?
questions.D4: How reliably can the clinic owner obtain an accurate count of completed treatment sessions for a selected week without manually counting individual entries?
questions.D5: How consistently does the clinic owner review workflow problems and assign corrective actions?

title: Information protection and recovery
description: How reliably clinic information is protected and can be recovered.

questions.E1: How consistently is access to patient information limited to staff who need it for their work?
questions.E2: How consistently are patient records protected from being viewed by visitors or other patients?
questions.E3: How reliably does your clinic maintain a separate recovery copy of essential patient and payment records?
questions.E4: How confidently can your clinic demonstrate that records can be recovered, based on an actual recovery check within the last six months?
questions.E5: How consistently is a departing staff member's access to clinic information removed promptly?
